🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico's ambassador walks into ICE detention centers</u>

Roberto Lazzeri, Mexico's ambassador to the US, went into Prairieland and Montgomery in Texas and Caroline in Virginia to check on Mexicans held by ICE. He also met ICE officials in Dallas, Houston and Atlanta to press for consular protection and dignified treatment.

The visit came as reports surfaced that 79 detainees in a Florida facility were locked in metal cages. Marking his first 100 days on the job, Lazzeri called the detention of Mexican migrants "the greatest tragedy" he has seen, and said defending the community is Sheinbaum's direct order.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>58 years after Tlatelolco: the CIA was funding Mexico's right-wing students</u>

On the eve of October 2, La Jornada reports on declassified files: the CIA ran at least five student projects in Mexico (LIHUFF, LICOAX, LIMIX, LIAGOG, LINOODLE) and had been bankrolling the far-right MURO since 1963. It also infiltrated FNET and Politécnico leadership while staying close to Gutiérrez Barrios and Nazar Haro's DFS.

National Security Archive researchers say that at best the Agency helped polarize student politics, and at worst it had "a more direct role in orchestrating the violence." Washington still keeps the key operational files from before the massacre censored.

🔥🇲🇽 "You come to power through electoral fraud, and then you talk about democracy?" — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 1, 2026 Former president Felipe Calderón reappeared on Sept 30 at a far-right forum, speaking about democracy, press freedom and organized crime. Sheinbaum recalled the 2006 fraud, his pacts with media owners, and that he made Genaro García Luna, later convicted in the US of taking cartel bribes, his Secretary of Public Security. "How is he not ashamed?" She also called Vicente Fox "a traitor to democracy" for promoting the 2005 desafuero against López Obrador and the 2006 fraud.

🇲🇽🕊️ "There is no repression from the Mexican State of any kind." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 1, 2026 On the eve of the 58th anniversary of the October 2, 1968 Tlatelolco massacre, Sheinbaum recalled that her government named Gustavo Díaz Ordaz as the one responsible, "because he himself acknowledged that he gave the order." An international right-wing event is being held freely in Mexico City, and Reforma ran "an absolute lie" on its front page today: "They even have the right to publish lies." Under Salinas de Gortari, more than 500 people were killed for political reasons. "How many are there now? None."

🇲🇽✊ "The pride of being Mexican is enormous. It wasn't like that in the neoliberal era." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 1, 2026 Asked about the contrast between the public response to Calderón and to López Obrador, who presented a new book on Sept 30, Sheinbaum first condemned any violence, including what was done to a Calderón statue at Los Pinos. She said the PRIAN is no longer widely accepted "because people's lives have changed, and so has their consciousness," and recalled the phrase "only the people can save the people." "Today we say it to the four winds: I am Mexican. That strength is invincible."

🇲🇽✊ "They took the Yaquis to Quintana Roo, to Yucatán, to be slaves during the Porfiriato on the henequen haciendas." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 1, 2026 Asked about her Sept 26 visit to Sonora, Sheinbaum recalled John Kenneth Turner's "Barbarous Mexico." Turner posed as a US hacienda owner in Yucatán and documented slavery that had been formally abolished since Vicente Guerrero. Many of the enslaved were Yaqui and Maya. Under the Yaqui Justice Plan, lands have been returned, water is reaching most communities, there is a university, and schools are being improved.

text: 🇲🇽💜 "There wasn't a single woman in the civic calendar, only men, as if there were only heroes and no heroines of the nation." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 1, 2026 On the second anniversary of taking office, Sheinbaum was asked what has changed for women. Today 24 women are in the civic calendar, and the mañanera's "Women in History" segment has presented 93 stories. She also cited the pension for women aged 60 to 64, equality written into the Constitution, and the new law on femicide. For girls and boys, she said, simply seeing a woman president "changes their mentality."
